title: AuthN/AuthZ Playbook Checklist
description: One entry per weakness pattern the invoking AI agent should look for when reviewing code for Broken Authentication / Broken Authorization (plan 023). Unlike detectors/secret or the planned detectors/code-review, this sub-skill has no deterministic scanner for most of cpmatch's stack (see plans/023-authn-authz-code-review-skill.md) — the agent reads this checklist and reasons over the code directly. A finding the agent produces from an item here must still conform to finding.schema.json.

ruleId.description: The ruleId the agent must stamp on any finding.schema.json finding it produces from this item — same naming convention as every other sub-skill (e.g. 'auth.missing-authorization-check').

guidance.description: Concrete instruction to the agent on what to look for in the code — not a restatement of the CWE definition.

evidenceRequirement.description: What counts as sufficient evidence before reporting this as a finding, not a suspicion — per the kickoff's evidentiary-rigor requirement (see meetings/2026-07-22-1500-plan-023-kickoff.md).

languageNotes.description: Optional per-language/framework idioms to check for (e.g. which decorator/middleware pattern to look for in that ecosystem). Not required for every item — the core guidance is language-agnostic; this only adds concrete, language-specific things to grep for.

references.description: Same shape as finding.schema.json's references[] — reused directly so an agent-produced finding's references can be copied straight from here.

suggestedSeverity.description: A default suggestion, not a hard rule (unlike 006, where severity is always Critical) — AuthN/AuthZ impact varies by what the exposed resource/action actually is. The agent may adjust based on context, but must not adjust silently: see confidenceGuidance.

defaultMax.description: Upper bound the agent should self-report for a playbook-derived finding of this item, absent stronger corroboration — deliberately lower than a deterministic detector's typical confidence (see kickoff: playbook findings carry the same evidentiary bar but inherently more reasoning uncertainty than a regex/AST match).
